title: The over-shared spreadsheet
brief: 16:50. Ruth in Sales needs “the customer list” for a board slide. The full export, 38,412 rows, is sitting in your Documents.
role: Accounts payable, with access to the customer export
insight: Most requests for “the list” need a number, not the list.
teaches: Ask what the data is for, then share the least that does the job
A count or a summary beats rows; masked columns beat full ones
Share through a controlled link, never “anyone with the link”

value.title: customers_full.xlsx
value.banner: Showing 5 of 38,412 rows. Personal data: handle under the privacy procedure.

messages.text: Hi Sam! Could you send me the customer list? Need it for tomorrow's board slide. Thanks!!

replies.text: Sure. What exactly do you need it to show?

value.title: Share customer data with Ruth (Sales)
body: Ruth needs customer data for a board slide. The source is customers_full.xlsx: 38,412 customers with names, contact details, dates of birth, home addresses and card endings.

policy.title: Veltrix privacy procedure, section 2
lines: Share the minimum personal data needed for the purpose. Prefer totals, then masked data, then full records.
Share internally through Filebridge, Veltrix only, with an expiry. Never by public link.

options.label: A table of customer counts and orders per region, no names
options.why: Everything the slide needs, and no one can be identified from it.

options.label: Rows with only region and orders, names removed
options.why: Acceptable, though a summary would have done.

options.label: Rows with names, emails and phone numbers, in case she needs them
options.why: “In case” is not a purpose. None of it goes on a board slide.

options.label: The whole export, it is quicker
options.why: 38,412 people's dates of birth, addresses and card endings, for a slide.

options.label: Filebridge link, Veltrix only, expiring in 7 days
options.why: Only staff, and it cleans itself up.

options.label: Attach it to an email
options.why: A copy in two mailboxes, forever, forwardable to anyone.

options.label: Filebridge link, anyone with the link
options.why: Anyone the link reaches can open it, with no sign in.

setup.title: Chat
setup.body: Ruth Adeyemi: could you send me the customer list?

outcome.label: Looked at what the export holds
outcome.what: Dates of birth, home addresses and card endings, for 38,412 people.
outcome.ideal: knows what is in a file before sharing it.

outcome.label: Asked what the data is for
outcome.what: Ruth only needs how many customers in each region ordered last month.
outcome.ideal: asks the purpose before sharing personal data.

message.text: Oh, just how many customers in each region ordered last month. One bar chart!

decide.objective: Give Ruth what she needs, and no more.
decide.insight: Ask what it is for, then share the smallest thing that does the job.

hint.text: Ask Ruth on the company chat what the slide needs. Then in the Work queue send counts per region, shared through a Veltrix only link with an expiry.

outcome.label: Shared the least that does the job
outcome.what: Ruth gets her bar chart. Nobody's personal data left the CRM.
outcome.ideal: minimises data and shares it through a controlled link.

card.title: One bar chart, zero people
body: Ruth asked for “the list” and needed a count. You sent the count, through a Veltrix only link that expires.
Every extra column you share is one more thing that can leak, be forwarded, or be kept for years.
card.ideal: asks the purpose and shares the minimum.

outcome.label: Sent the full customer export
outcome.what: 38,412 people's personal data went out for one slide. If that link or email travels, it is a breach.
outcome.ideal: never sends a full export when a summary will do.

card.title: The whole list, for one slide
body: Names, dates of birth, home addresses and card endings for every customer are now sitting in another place, for a bar chart.
The purpose was a count by region. That is what should have been sent.
card.ideal: shares totals, not people, when totals do the job.

outcome.label: Shared it with a public link
outcome.what: Anyone with the link can open it, with no sign in, for as long as the link lives.
outcome.ideal: shares internally with a restricted, expiring link.

card.title: Anyone with the link
body: A public link does not stay with the person you sent it to. It gets forwarded, pasted and indexed.
Veltrix only, with an expiry, costs nothing extra.
card.ideal: never shares personal data by public link.

outcome.label: Shared more than was needed
outcome.what: Ruth got more personal data than the slide needs, or a copy that will live in mailboxes.
outcome.ideal: shares the minimum through a controlled link.

card.title: More than the job needed
body: Nothing terrible, but more personal data now lives in more places than the purpose required. Open the case to see which choice was off.
card.ideal: asks what the data is for, and sends the minimum.
